public_rationale: On August 7, 2025, OpenAI reported nearly 700 million weekly ChatGPT users, showing substantial actual use [e1]. Ramp's September 9 report put AI adoption in its observed business population at 44.5% for August 2025 and described growth in businesses paying for subscriptions [e2]. These usage and paid-adoption measures contradict the general absence of meaningful AI demand [e1] [e2]. They do not establish whether demand justifies the infrastructure investment described [e1] [e2].
limitations: The weekly usage figure does not distinguish free from paid users [e1].
Ramp's result describes its observed business population, not all businesses [e2].
Usage and subscription adoption do not establish profitability or adequate infrastructure investment returns [e1] [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There really isn't any demand for AI in general, let alone at the scale of the hundreds of billions of dollars being sunk into it.

statement.excerpt: As I discussed a month or so ago, data center development accounted for more of America’s GDP growth than all consumer spending combined, and there really isn’t any demand for AI in general, let alone at the scale that these hundreds of billions of dollars are being sunk into.

from_speaker: there really isn’t any demand for AI in general
hundreds of billions of dollars being sunk into
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is an absence of meaningful AI demand, rather than a literal claim that no individual uses AI.
Use August 2025, the latest completed calendar month before publication, for the ongoing demand observation.
Substantial actual use and paid adoption can refute the general absence claim without proving that infrastructure investment is economically justified.
The GDP-growth clause is outside the supplied normalized proposition and is not graded here.
This is an industry demand claim, not a specific company revenue figure; metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence shows negligible actual use and paid adoption, together with demand insufficient to sustain the infrastructure scale described.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated evidence shows substantial actual AI adoption and paid demand, contradicting the asserted general absence. This does not by itself contradict the narrower concern about investment adequacy.

evidence.explanation: The company reported substantial actual usage during the target month. This contradicts an absence of meaningful demand, but does not establish paid demand or profitability.
